glasswing_sardine.name: Glasswing Sardine
glasswing_sardine.lore: Schools of them skip over the surface like thrown pebbles.
glasswing_sardine.hint: Watch for skipping flashes over the shallows.
glasswing_sardine.signature: body clear as blown glass with one glowing spine line; long wing-like pectoral fins

driftback.name: Driftback
driftback.lore: It lies still among the real driftwood, then bolts.
driftback.hint: Some of the driftwood by the pier is not driftwood.
driftback.signature: a twisted sun-bleached driftwood branch: grain for scales, knot-holes for eyes, dried-seaweed dorsal fronds

compass_flounder.name: Compass Flounder
compass_flounder.hint: Lies flat on the sandy bottom. Sandworms bring it up.
compass_flounder.signature: round flat disc divided into a compass rose by raised bone ridges; needle-spine on its back turns to point north

shellback_blenny.name: Shellback Blenny
shellback_blenny.lore: It bites the hook, then retreats into its shell.
shellback_blenny.hint: Hides in a spiral shell near the rocks. Be patient.
shellback_blenny.signature: lives in a spiral seashell like a hermit crab; only a frilled head and fins stick out

kelp_wraith.name: Kelp Wraith
kelp_wraith.lore: Invisible in the kelp until it moves.
kelp_wraith.hint: Cast into the kelp beds. Its float-bulbs glow at dusk.
kelp_wraith.signature: body built from overlapping kelp blades; amber float-bulbs along the spine glow at dusk

seaglass_puffer.name: Seaglass Puffer
seaglass_puffer.lore: The tide polished it for a hundred years.
seaglass_puffer.hint: Something glints green among the pebbles. Glass shrimp, perhaps.
seaglass_puffer.signature: body is a cluster of frosted sea-glass shards; inflating spreads them into a spiky glass sphere

old_mooring.name: The Old Mooring
old_mooring.lore: The one that got away, for fifty years.
old_mooring.hint: Every angler on the cove has lost a hook to it. Try the deep water off the end of the pier.
old_mooring.signature: huge catfish; barbels are frayed mooring ropes, iron ring through its lip, jaw bristling with old hooks and lures, barnacle-crusted tar-black hide

sailcloth_ray.name: Sailcloth Ray
sailcloth_ray.lore: Born from a mainsail that tore loose in a gale; it still flies the shallows at high tide.
sailcloth_ray.hint: Square shadows gliding over the sandbar are not sails.
sailcloth_ray.signature: its wings ARE patched canvas sailcloth: stitched seams, a darker patch, grommet holes along the wing edge, a frayed rope bridle for a tail

knotted_needlefish.name: Knotted Needlefish
knotted_needlefish.lore: Tied itself in knots escaping a net and never untied.
knotted_needlefish.hint: Thin as a rope end, quick as a whip, just under the surface.
knotted_needlefish.signature: slender body braided from tight sailor's knot-work cord (a monkey's-fist knot at the head), its beak a steel marlinspike

lampfin_gurnard.name: Lampfin Gurnard
lampfin_gurnard.lore: Walks the seabed at dusk on finger-fins, its wings lit like a harbour lamp.
lampfin_gurnard.hint: Look for a warm light crawling along the bottom at dusk.
lampfin_gurnard.signature: huge fan pectoral fins ARE oiled-paper lantern panes in thin soot-black frames, lit amber from within; walks on three finger-rays

oyster_hoarder.name: Oyster Hoarder
oyster_hoarder.lore: Keeps the cove's pearls in its cheeks. Land one and it pays a pearl.
oyster_hoarder.hint: A heavy, slow shadow near the rocks that glints when it turns.
oyster_hoarder.signature: stocky wrasse whose cheeks and gill plates ARE half-open oyster shells, nacre inside, pearls showing in the gaps; ridged shell-scale back

moonwake_ribbonfish.name: Moonwake Ribbonfish
moonwake_ribbonfish.lore: The strip of moonlight on the water at night, sometimes, is a fish.
moonwake_ribbonfish.hint: At night, a silver ribbon on the dark water that doesn't follow the moon.
moonwake_ribbonfish.signature: very long ribbon body that IS a strip of moonlit wake: rippling silver light with a crimson crest running its whole length, no visible scales

bottlepost_wrasse.name: Bottle-post Wrasse
bottlepost_wrasse.lore: Swallowed a message in a bottle and became one. Nobody has read the note yet.
bottlepost_wrasse.hint: A green glint bobbing between the rocks, like a bottle that swims.
bottlepost_wrasse.signature: body IS a sea-green message bottle: thick translucent glass flanks with a rolled, sealed letter visible inside, a cork for a snout, wax-seal red gill flash

saltcrust_sole.name: Saltcrust Sole
saltcrust_sole.lore: Lay so long in a drying tide pool the salt grew over it like frost.
saltcrust_sole.hint: A pale patch on the sandy bottom that cracks when it moves.
saltcrust_sole.signature: flat oval body crusted with white salt crystals in a cracked hexagon salt-flat pattern, rust-orange showing through the cracks; edge fins fringed with crystal

spindrift_flyingfish.name: Spindrift Flyingfish
spindrift_flyingfish.lore: Born where the wind tears the tops off the waves. It flies further than it swims.
spindrift_flyingfish.hint: Out past the island, little silver darts skipping over the swell.
spindrift_flyingfish.signature: long pectoral wings ARE sheets of wind-torn sea-foam lace, translucent and frayed at the edges; slim cobalt body

signalflag_tuna.name: Signal-flag Tuna
signalflag_tuna.lore: Schools of them run the open sea like a fleet, finlets flying the old harbour code.
signalflag_tuna.hint: Fast shadows in a line far off the island. They hit hard and run.
signalflag_tuna.signature: the row of finlets along its back and belly ARE tiny maritime signal pennants in the harbour code (yellow, blue, red, chequered), stiff like real finlets; steel-blue torpedo body

hullback_sunfish.name: Hullback Sunfish
hullback_sunfish.lore: Basks on the swell like a capsized boat. Sailors have tried to tie up to it.
hullback_sunfish.hint: A great round shape lying flat on the open sea, one round eye glowing.
hullback_sunfish.signature: huge round mola body IS a section of clinker-built ship's hull: overlapping tarred planks for scales, barnacle crusts, a brass-rimmed porthole for an eye glowing amber

rigging_shark.name: Rigging Shark
rigging_shark.lore: The ghost of a ship that sank with all sails set. It still hunts the deep water off the cove.
rigging_shark.hint: Far out, in the deepest water: a long pale shape with a green light running along its side.
rigging_shark.signature: fog-grey translucent skin over a skeleton of ship's rigging: wooden spars for ribs, taut hemp ropes for sinews, its dorsal fin a torn topsail on a spar; a lantern-green glow along the lateral line

mossneck.name: Mossneck
mossneck.lore: The old causeway to the cove sank a thousand years ago. Some say it never sank: it swam.
mossneck.hint: Three humps far out on a calm sea, and a long neck rising like a mooring post.
mossneck.signature: a long-necked sea serpent whose humps ARE mossy drowned stone arches of an ancient causeway, neck a weathered barnacled mooring column wrapped in frayed rope, small head with lantern-green eyes

anchorjaw_leviathan.name: Anchorjaw Leviathan
anchorjaw_leviathan.lore: Every ship that dropped anchor over it lost the anchor. It wears them all.
anchorjaw_leviathan.hint: A shadow as long as the pier, and the sound of chain dragging under the water.
anchorjaw_leviathan.signature: a colossal grouper whose lower jaw is a row of rusted ship's anchors for teeth, anchor chains trailing from its lip like barbels, hull-plate scales riveted and barnacled

drowned_lighthouse.name: The Drowned Lighthouse
drowned_lighthouse.lore: A lighthouse fell into the sea in a storm and kept its light on. At night its beam still sweeps the water, looking for ships.
drowned_lighthouse.hint: At night, far out, a slow beam of light turning under the waves.
drowned_lighthouse.signature: a giant sea eel whose head IS a ruined lighthouse lantern room (cracked glass panes, brass frame, a burning lamp inside throwing a beam), its body courses of mossy whitewashed stone blocks banded with red

barnacle_rockling.name: Barnacle Rockling
barnacle_rockling.lore: Sat still on the same rock so long the barnacles took it for a rock.
barnacle_rockling.hint: A rock near the shore that blinks.
barnacle_rockling.signature: small stocky fish crusted all over in live barnacles that open and close like breathing little mouths; slate body showing between them

shingle_skipper.name: Shingle Skipper
shingle_skipper.lore: Tiled in beach pebbles. It skips across the shallows like a thrown stone.
shingle_skipper.hint: Pebbles on the sandy bottom that suddenly scatter.
shingle_skipper.signature: small flat fish whose back is a mosaic of smooth rounded beach pebbles, set like tiles, sea-green grout between them

chartline_mackerel.name: Chartline Mackerel
chartline_mackerel.lore: Its stripes are the tide lines of a chart nobody has drawn yet.
chartline_mackerel.hint: Out past the shore, fast blue shoals that turn all at once.
chartline_mackerel.signature: sleek mackerel whose back stripes ARE inked depth-contour lines of a sea chart, wavy and numbered, over deep blue; silver belly

tallow_candlefish.name: Tallow Candlefish
tallow_candlefish.lore: So oily the old fishers dried them and lit them like candles. They still glow at dusk.
tallow_candlefish.hint: At dusk, a shoal of tiny flames under the water.
tallow_candlefish.signature: slender pale fish of dripping ivory tallow wax, its dorsal fin a lit wick with a small flame (glow only there)

inkwell_cuttlefin.name: Inkwell Cuttlefin
inkwell_cuttlefin.lore: Fell from a captain's desk in a storm and learned to swim. Scare it and it clouds the water.
inkwell_cuttlefin.hint: A dark cloud blooming in the water where a fish just was.
inkwell_cuttlefin.signature: rounded body IS a thick glass inkwell full of swirling navy ink, brass collar at the neck, fin frills of ink-stained paper

bellows_grouper.name: Bellows Grouper
bellows_grouper.lore: Breathes like a forge. You hear it before you see it.
bellows_grouper.hint: A heavy shape by the rocks and bubbles puffing up in rhythm.
bellows_grouper.signature: heavy grouper whose gill covers ARE leather forge bellows with brass studs that pump in and out, soot-dark scales with ember-orange edges

weathervane_gar.name: Weathervane Gar
weathervane_gar.lore: Always points into the wind. Sailors read the weather off it.
weathervane_gar.hint: A long thin shadow on the surface, all pointing the same way.
weathervane_gar.signature: long thin gar whose snout IS a copper weathervane arrow with its tail fletching, scales like overlapping grey roof slates

glassfloat_jelly.name: Glassfloat Jelly
glassfloat_jelly.lore: A fisherman's glass net float that broke loose and grew a life of its own.
glassfloat_jelly.hint: A honey-coloured bubble drifting just under the surface.
glassfloat_jelly.signature: bell IS a hand-blown amber glass net float with tiny trapped air bubbles, wrapped in a net of knotted cord; tentacles are trailing net cords glowing faintly at the tips

reefbeak_parrotfish.name: Reefbeak Parrotfish
reefbeak_parrotfish.lore: It eats coral and turns into it. The oldest ones are more reef than fish.
reefbeak_parrotfish.hint: By the rocks in daylight, a fish that looks like a piece of the reef.
reefbeak_parrotfish.signature: parrotfish whose body IS a living branching coral knot, coral-orange with sea-purple polyps, its beak white bleached coral

keelback_sawfish.name: Keelback Sawfish
keelback_sawfish.lore: Grew a keel instead of a snout. Wrecks have been found cut clean in two.
keelback_sawfish.hint: A long flat shadow on the sandy bottom with a straight beam in front.
keelback_sawfish.signature: flat sawfish whose long rostrum IS an oak ship keel timber sheathed in green copper, the saw teeth copper nails; oak-brown back

diamond_coelacanth.name: Diamond Coelacanth
diamond_coelacanth.lore: Older than the island. Every century under the pressure of the deep turned another scale to diamond.
diamond_coelacanth.hint: Only far out, in the deepest water: a slow old fish that throws back the light like cut glass.
diamond_coelacanth.signature: an ancient lobe-finned coelacanth whose heavy armour scales ARE cut diamonds, faceted and throwing prism sparkles, on a deep midnight-blue body; lobed fins like stubby legs

golden_eel.name: Golden Eel
golden_eel.lore: Swam through a sunken treasure ship's hold for a hundred years and came out gold.
golden_eel.hint: Far from the island, a ribbon of gold winding through deep water.
golden_eel.signature: a long eel whose skin IS hammered gold leaf, rippled and burnished, with darker antique-gold edges and black-pearl eyes; a faint warm gleam along its back
